newsitem.title: USA: REPUBLIC HELPED BY LIFO,LOWER SCRAP PRICES.
newsitem.headline: REPUBLIC HELPED BY LIFO,LOWER SCRAP PRICES.

text.p: Republic Engineered Steels Inc Wednesday reported a fourth quarter profit before special charges, citing a LIFO credit and lower scrap prices.

For the quarter ended June 30, Republic reported adjusted net income -- excluding the after-tax effect of non-cash ESOP and special charges -- of $1,108,000 compared with a year earlier loss excluding special items of $3,275,000.
Net sales for the quarter were $198,830,000 on shipments of 270,911 tons, a 3.3 percent increase from sales revenues of $192,494,000 on shipments of 241,298 tons for the 1996 fourth fiscal quarter.

Republic said the revenue increase is the result of a 12.3 percent rise in shipping volume, despite falling selling prices and a lower percentage of sales of higher priced value-added products. Average selling prices fell to $734 per ton from $798 per ton or about 8.0 percent.
It said the product mix change is primarily a function of greater shipments of hot rolled semi-finished steels and a corresponding decrease in specialty semi-finished sales to converters.

"Despite the company's improved operating performance in the fourth quarter," Chief Executive Officer Russell Maier said, "the financial results were benefitted by factors which may not recur. A LIFO credit of $3.9 million and a decrease in scrap prices of almost seven percent significantly helped quarterly results."

The company said its Cast-Roll facility continues its steady movement toward optimum operation. During the fourth quarter, 53 percent of Republic's SBQ -- special bar quality -- production was made by way of the Cast-Roll route.
That represents 85 percent of the facility's capacity, up from 59 percent a year ago, Maier said.
The company said it negotiated a new three-year revolving credit facility of $115 million during the quarter "on more favorable terms than the facility it replaced."
As of June 30, it added, nothing was outstanding against the credit.

"Over the past months, Republic management has worked with leading steel industry financial, marketing and technical advisors, as well as representatives of the United Steelworkers of America, in an effort to develop means and methods for generating needed funding to install capital to enhance productivity and quality, while reducing operating costs," Mair said.

He said these efforts are consistent with previously announced authorization from directors to proceed with planning and engineering work on a new bar rolling mill, adding that work continues and is nearing completion.
